negative_findings.description: No HU systemic bank was found to publish a standing, machine-readable series of card counts, ATM fleet size or POS terminal counts. Where such figures appear, they are prose or chart values inside PDF annual reports and investor decks, and definitions differ per bank.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches in Hungarian for 'bankkártya darabszám', 'ATM hálózat', 'kártyaforgalom' returned report landing pages and PDFs, never a data table or API.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any cross-bank card/ATM/POS series must be hand-normalised from PDFs; the pipeline needs PDF table/OCR extraction plus a per-bank definition map, not a feed reader.

negative_findings.description: No dedicated 'digital bank KPI deck' was found for the unlisted HU banks (K&H, Erste HU, Raiffeisen HU, UniCredit HU, CIB). Only OTP, MBH and Gránit run genuine investor-presentation programmes; the other five publish statutory reports only.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches for 'befektetői prezentáció' plus each bank name surfaced statutory reports and parent-group material, not subsidiary KPI decks.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Digital-payment KPIs for over half the cell must be sourced indirectly from parent groups or media, lowering comparability and timeliness.

negative_findings.description: No stable Hungarian bank-side term was found for merchant-acquiring volume equivalent to 'POS acquiring volume'. Candidate phrasings ('elfogadói forgalom', 'kártyaelfogadás', 'POS terminál darabszám') were used but did not surface bank-published acquiring statistics in this cell's searches.
negative_findings.result_summary: Acquiring-side terminology appears to live with the regulator and with acquirer/PSP entities rather than in bank IR language.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Acquiring coverage for this cell is likely unreachable from bank IR alone and must be triangulated with regulator and PSP-side cells.

negative_findings.description: Two commercially useful aggregators are restricted: OPTEN company reports are paid, and portfolio.hu's deeper bank analysis sits behind Portfolio Premium. The e-beszamolo bulk dataset is likewise only available via a paid/requested data-supply route, not by scraping.
negative_findings.result_summary: Paywall and bulk-data-request models observed on opten.hu, portfolio.hu/premium and e-beszamolo 'beszámoló állomány értékesítése'.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Budget and licensing decisions are needed if systematic cross-bank financial normalisation is wanted; free routes cover primary documents only.

negative_findings.description: Parent-group IR portals (KBC, Erste Group, RBI, Intesa Sanpaolo, UniCredit Group) were inferred from ownership structure and included with root-level URLs only; they were not fetched in this run.
negative_findings.result_summary: URLs supplied as high-confidence-but-unverified starting points, not as confirmed live pages.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The deterministic verification pass should resolve these and locate the exact Hungary-segment report paths before they are relied upon.

coverage_gaps.description: Bank-owned payment subsidiaries and acquiring arms were not separately scouted in this run — notably OTP Mobil (SimplePay), OTP's merchant-acquiring unit, and any MBH/Erste payment service entities. These file their own statutory accounts and often disclose transaction volumes their parent bank does not.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a dedicated pass on bank-owned PSP/acquirer subsidiaries via e-beszamolo entity search plus HU searches on 'OTP Mobil', 'SimplePay', 'kártyaelfogadás', 'elfogadóhely'.

coverage_gaps.description: Cash usage from the bank side (ATM cash withdrawal volumes, branch cash handling, cash-recycler deployment) was not located in any bank-published source found here; banks disclose network size but not cash throughput.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Cross-check against the MNB payment-systems cell; from this cell, target ATM network commentary and Pillar 3 operational sections as the only bank-side proxy.

coverage_gaps.description: ESEF/iXBRL filings (observed for OTP and UniCredit Jelzálogbank) were noted but not evaluated for whether they carry any of the operational KPIs of interest; they are structured but likely financial-statement-only.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Test-parse one ESEF package per bank to decide whether structured extraction is worth building versus PDF extraction.

coverage_gaps.description: Only three of the eight cell banks publish quarterly; the rest are annual-only, so any bank-side card/digital series will be annual with a 3-5 month publication lag.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Anchor the cell's expected cadence at annual, and use parent-group quarterly segment reporting plus press releases for intra-year signal.

coverage_gaps.description: Several HU banks publish HU and EN versions of the same report with differing detail; it was not established which language version is authoritative or more complete per bank.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: For each bank, compare one HU/EN report pair and record which version to collect.

brief: Hungary's systemic bank issuers/acquirers split into two disclosure regimes: three genuine investor-communicating banks (OTP, MBH, Gránit) that publish quarterly reports and KPI-bearing investor decks, and five foreign-owned subsidiaries (K&H, Erste HU, Raiffeisen HU, UniCredit HU, CIB) that publish only statutory annual and Pillar 3 reports, with their Hungarian digital/card KPIs surfacing instead in parent-group segment reporting. Three pointer hubs make the cell tractable and should be the collection backbone: the BÉT/BSE kibinfo archive, the MNB tőkepiaci közzétételek portal, and the Ministry of Justice e-beszámoló register, each of which mirrors bank filings more durably than the banks' own CMS. The operational metrics this workstream wants — card counts, ATM fleet size, POS/acquiring volumes, mobile-wallet adoption — exist only as prose or chart values inside PDFs, with per-bank definitions, so the pipeline needs PDF/deck extraction and a normalisation map rather than any feed. Acquiring-side and cash-throughput figures were not found on the bank side at all and will have to come from the regulator and PSP cells.
